Respiratory Follow-up Clinic Letter

Dear Doctor,

Re: Patient seen in clinic following recent admission with COVID-19 pneumonia.

The patient was discharged from hospital at 02:41 on 22/03/2020 following an admission for COVID-19 pneumonia.
for COVID-19 pneumonia confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 21:56 on 04/03/2020, result reported 23:53 on 04/03/2020), complicated by hypoxia requiring supplemental oxygen during admission. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis was given during admission.

The patient was seen in follow-up clinic at 19:19 on 31/03/2020.

Current symptoms: Mild residual fatigue and occasional external breathlessness, both improving. No cough, chest pain, calf swelling or symptoms suggestive of venous thromboembolism.

Examination: SpO2 97% on air, RR 15/min, chest clear to auscultation bilaterally, no signs of respiratory distress.

Investigations: Chest X-ray in clinic showed near-complete resolution of previous basal changes.
Bloods showed normal inflammatory markers and renal function.

Plan: Reassured regarding good clinical and radiological recovery. Advised to continue gradual return to normal activity, including work and exercise as tolerated. No further respiratory follow-up required unless symptoms recur, in which case could welcome re-referral.

Please continue to support recovery in primary care.

Yours sincerely, Respiratory Medicine Team
